body:
As far as I understand it, this is expected. The behavior in the video has nothing to do with `locale/fallback`.

You may have misunderstood how `locale/fallback` works. **Godot will not skip translation when the current locale and `locale/fallback` are the same.** It's when all currently loaded translation files cannot provide translations for the current locale, that the translation server will attempt to use the locale in `locale/fallback` to translate _again_.

Your MRP's behavior looks strange because the PO for `en_US` was added to the `TranslationServer` at runtime, and after adding it you didn't manually trigger a global update (e.g., switching the locale, or emitting the `NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED` signal), so the label initially shows `show en`. If you add the PO file to the project settings, or swap the two lines in your `_ready` function, you'll see it initially shows `show en_US`.

But indeed, for example, developing in `zh_Hans` but needing to add `zh_Hant` localization is a common requirement (at least in China). `locale/fallback` was originally designed for inter-language fallback I guess. We may need to add additional settings to address this situation, e.g., add a setting to switch the behavior to skipping translation when fallback locale matches the current locale.

> Your MRP's behavior looks strange because the PO for `en_US` was added to the `TranslationServer` at runtime, and after adding it you didn't manually trigger a global update (e.g., switching the locale, or emitting the `NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED` signal), so the label initially shows `show en`. If you add the PO file to the project settings, or swap the two lines in your `_ready` function, you'll see it initially shows `show en_US`.

Yes, I am aware of that. In MRP, the `load` function is intentionally used to load PO files, which is done to better illustrate the issue.

> But indeed, for example, developing in zh_Hans but needing to add zh_Hant localization is a common requirement (at least in China). locale/fallback was originally designed for inter-language fallback I guess. We may need to add additional settings to address this situation, e.g., add a setting to switch the behavior to skipping translation when fallback locale matches the current locale.

Agree to add an extra option. I think it could work as follows: when enabled, if the current locale equals the fallback locale, `TranslationDomain::get_message_from_translations` will only use translations that exactly match the current locale. If no such translation exists, it will directly return the original text.

It should not completely skip translation when the current locale equals the fallback locale, because many built-in texts are in `en` (such as various context menu pop-ups). Completely skipping translation would cause translations added for built-in texts to be skipped as well.

The current translation retrieval logic is more friendly to using keywords as translation keys (the original text is only used when there is no translation in any similar locale). However, it becomes much more complex when using the original text as translation keys.
